newsitem.title: USA: U.S., Japan see key differences in insurance talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan see key differences in insurance talks.

text.p: Senior U.S. and Japanese negotiators meeting in San Francisco said on Saturday major hurdles remained to an agreement to open up Japan's insurance market.
"There's a significant distance that we're working on," said U.S. trade negotiator Ira Shapiro after the first half of Saturday's talks. "We have a distance to cover."
His Japanese counterpart in the talks, Eisuke Sakakibara, said: "The differences are still very large."
They would not elaborate on the sticking points.

Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, Shapiro and other trade negotiators resumed their two-day talks earlier on Saturday in a race to settle their differences ahead of the Dec. 15 deadline.
Sakakibara said earlier that Dec. 15 remained Tokyo's target, but he described the San Francisco talks thus far as "rough sailing."

At issue is Japan's $382 billion domestic insurance market. Washington is pressing Japan to liberalize its primary insurance markets before a niche area called the "Third Sector," where U.S. firms have been dominant, is opened up to Japanese insurers.
The Third Sector includes areas such as personal accident, illness and nursing care, and stand-alone cancer policies.
The dispute has become a major trade irritant between the two countries. They had originally set a July 31 deadline to settle the dispute, but recently agreed to push back the deadline to Dec. 15.
